title: Wanderings in Balochistan (Annotated)
author: charles-metcalfe-macgregor

description.short: Across Balochistan, the next well can matter more than the next frontier.
description.long:
Across Balochistan, the next well can matter more than the next frontier.

Charles Metcalfe MacGregor follows the tracks inland from the coast, through ravines, stony plains and mountain passes. Camels, grazing, local guides and the uncertain supply of water give his journey its daily measure. His eye moves between the appearance of the landscape and the practical question of how it can be crossed.

First published in 1882, Wanderings in Balochistan joins a soldier-geographer's travel narrative to detailed descriptions of routes. Behind its particulars lies the frontier world of the Great Game: Persia, Afghanistan and British India, and the growing strategic importance of geographical knowledge.

MacGregor's observations restore human scale to that wide map. The country emerges one march, one ridge and one negotiation at a time.
